newsitem.title: FRANCE: Paris airports delay Latin American trip.
newsitem.headline: Paris airports delay Latin American trip.

text.p: A visit to Latin America by a task force from the Paris airports (ADP) has been delayed by three months until December.

The main aim of the trip is to promote the Paris airports as a gateway for air cargo with freight forwarders and other industry professionals as well as shippers, a spokesman for ADP's freight marketing department told Reuters.
"The new dates for the trip are December 8 to 10 with visits to Sao Paulo (Brazil), Buenos Aires (Argentina) and Santiago (Chile)," he added.
All three cities are served with scheduled air cargo services by Air France.

"This will be the task force's first trip to Latin America, a region which generates relatively minor air cargo volumes in relation to North America and the Far East but whose rate of growth is among the strongest in the industry," the spokesman said.
The task force will include representatives from ADP, Air France Cargo, French agents association, SNAGFA as well as customs.
The task force has also re-arranged a U.S. visit to October 22 to 28 when it will go to Houston, Atlanta and Miami.
"We had scheduled the trip for early November or just after the Air Cargo Americas trade fair in Miami but on reflection decided it would be better to conduct it before this event takes place."

"Atlanta and Houston are respectively the hubs of Delta and Continental and the two airlines' alliances with Air France, which includes freight traffic, will provide the backdrop to the task force' visit," the spokesman said.
Air France operates scheduled cargo services to Miami and Houston and ad hoc full-freighters to Atlanta. - Reuters Air Cargo Service Tel+ 44 171 542 7706 Fax +5017
